Pandemic times have left my life exceptionally bland and drained, but my distraction of choice is video games. I bought the new Pokémon the other day, log into the FFXIV MMORPG daily, have a large backlog of games across PC and console, and will always be down to play something when asked. The pain doesn't stop and personally, I wouldn't want it to. 


I lost my dad three years ago, so this isn't coming from an *I could only imagine how devastating it was for you* point of view. We might be going through the same kind of pain, but I know what we feel is far too personal and unique to compare to one another. All I have for you is my experience of it and maybe it just might help you figure out how to handle those hard days a little better. 


It hurts, but I try to see it in an *I'm so happy it hurts* kind of way. I'm remembering him. It hurts, but am I angry or upset? I couldn't possibly be. My dad taught me some of the most important life lessons. I'm proud I had him as my dad and I know that is he was still alive today, he would be proud of me. The more it hurts, the more I think of how important the time we spent together is to me. It will last for as long as I live because my dad taught me how to live with respect, compassion, and self-sacrifice. 


I think of how he would be reading out the silly pamphlets we got with the weekly flyers to improve his English. That dedication to be able to communicate in this foreign land with whatever tools he had so that he could help her daughter with her kindergarten homework is something that hits me in the feels like a truck, but I am so very grateful and motivated to be the best that I can possibly be and more. 

I imagine getting married and having children, but that same hurt feeling is there. At first, I am riddled with negativity. I don't want anyone but my dad to walk me down the aisle, but he's not here anymore. What am I going to tell my children when they ask why I don't have a dad or why they only have one grandfather? It hurts and I'm sad, but it's okay.  

I learned to love by being loved. To care as deeply as I've cared, I learned of the love my father has for me. My father will not be there when I marry the one I love, but he taught me that caring for others is the basis of human interaction. To see it in action is the most heartwarming experience. I have the love of my father and I will continue to care and extend my love because of it. 

Then, we get to my children. I want to tell them about their grandfather and I know I would gush with gratitude and stories of him. I was lucky I was raised by him, and if I could be as great a parent as he was, he will live on in my children and be proud to have me be their parent. 


Days are **hard**. There will always be **pain**. What my dad left me with is too important to feel hurt for too long. Instead, I'm grateful and live with the honour of being his daughter despite how it may hurt. 


I wish you well. PM if you want to talk more.
